title: GRAPE: Gradient Refinement and Progress-Aware Exploitation for Query-Efficient High-Dimensional Bayesian Optimization
abstract: arXiv:2608.25116v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Optimizing expensive, high-dimensional black-box functions remains a central challenge in modern machine learning and scientific discovery. While local Bayesian optimization mitigates the curse of dimensionality, existing techniques often prioritize the probability of descent over the magnitude of progress. This leads to overly conservative steps that yield negligible improvement, wasting queries on directions that are nearly certain to descend but offer little decrease. We introduce Gradient Refinement and Progress-Aware Exploitation (GRAPE), a two-stage framework that first sharpens the local gradient posterior via a closed-form acquisition function, then selects update directions by maximizing the expected decrease conditional on descent. translated_title: GRAPE：梯度细化与进度感知利用，用于查询高效的高维贝叶斯优化
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.25116v1 公告类型：新 摘要：优化昂贵的高维黑箱函数仍然是现代机器学习和科学发现中的核心挑战。尽管局部贝叶斯优化缓解了维度灾难问题，但现有技术往往优先考虑下降概率而非下降幅度。这导致采取过于保守的步骤，仅产生微不足道的改进，将查询浪费在几乎确定会下降但收益甚微的方向上。我们引入了梯度细化与进度感知利用（GRAPE），这是一个两阶段框架，首先通过闭式采集函数锐化局部梯度后验，然后通过最大化条件于下降的期望减少来选择更新方向。理论分析证明，该梯度细化阶段单调地最小化局部不确定性，并且随着后验形状的演变，进度感知方向收敛到真正的陡峭下降方向。
tldr: GRAPE通过两阶段框架，先锐化局部梯度后验，再基于期望下降幅度选择更新方向，从而在高维贝叶斯优化中避免保守步骤，实现更高效的查询利用。
en_tdlr: GRAPE employs a two-stage framework that sharpens local gradient posterior and selects update directions based on expected decrease magnitude, avoiding conservative steps for more query-efficient high-dimensional Bayesian optimization.
